scope: Independent drag-input + Preview/offline mount hook review only
conclusion: No remaining blocking defect confirmed in the scoped current host paths after the parent click-suppression fix.

hooks.text: const schedule = () => { if (drag?.hasActiveDrag() && !runtime.state().motionState?.drag?.started) drag.cancel(); if (!renderPending) { renderPending = true; queueMicrotask(safeRender); } };

findings.location: src/runtime/drag-input.ts hasActiveDrag; Preview subscribe; mountOfflinePrototype schedule
findings.detail: The controller ends its active session before arming same-target mouse click suppression. A blanket idle cancel clears that pending suppression. The current hosts cancel only an active bridge when core drag is no longer started. Four module/serialized+host cases verify a later idle notification/releasePointerStyles does not erase suppression; next click is prevented and unregisters the listener.

Actual core page navigation and deletion of an already rendered row stop the active bridge, remove movement/up listeners, restore the body cursor and allow the next page source to begin. Touch cancellation similarly clears touch listeners without invoking Drop; removal during Drop does not leave body cursor stuck.

Controlled pagehide({persisted:true}) leaves Preview active if neither blur nor unmount occurs. Offline pagehide permanently disposes its controller and has no pageshow rebind, so a persisted document cannot start a new drag after pageshow. BFCache eligibility for these Electron/file/embedded hosts was not established. If persisted restoration is a supported surface, cancel on persisted pagehide or explicitly recreate on pageshow; validate in a real eligible browser history traversal before claiming fixed.

failureHistory.cause: Row fixtures had not called runtime.widget before drag, unlike both real hosts; missing renderedContexts prevented the simulated deleted-row cleanup. Core whole-file hash changed while this initial run was active.

failureHistory.correction: Added actual host render precondition runtime.widget(box,context); switched from Vite SSR fixture constructors to minimal independent records and direct TS module imports; no dev server needed. No product edits.

limitations: No browser was opened or real pointer/touch/BFCache transition performed. The current product bridge and exact current host subscription expressions executed with a controlled document/event surface and the actual core runtime.
Portable coverage serializes bindRuntimeDrag only. Whole offline HTML/frame bootstrap serialization is outside this narrow review; parent browser/export regression owns that coverage.

The core export-runtime.ts was changing during initial review. Initial and corrected before/after hashes are retained; corrected20-case execution had no source drift. This is not a fresh review of the entire motion planner.
Original drag.js corroboration is the frozen52-case retained-source report; it proves modern non-IE target equality and next-click suppression, but not pagehide/BFCache lifecycle.
Multi-touch identity follows changedTouches[0] as the retained source does. No claim of robust multi-pointer ownership or real touch-device scrolling is made.

Row-removal cleanup requires the actual host precondition of rendering/registering the row instance. The first harness omitted runtime.widget and observed four failures; this is preserved as a harness-scope error, not a user-visible product defect.
